Subject: FedRAMP / ISO control owner mapping and evidence timeline

Hi Irene,

We're working toward an internal procurement deadline and need to validate Redwood's posture across several artifacts (SOC 2, SIG/CAIQ, ISO 27001, and FedRAMP). Two quick asks:  

1) Can you share a mapping of control owners and a short list of representative evidence (logs, policies, configuration screenshots) we can include in our packet? Prefer CSV/XLS.
2) We have an upcoming audit window on Nov 20 and need the questionnaire completed and evidence delivered by Nov 10. Where are you on ISO 27001 plans and FedRAMP readiness? Specifically: Moderate or Low baseline? Do you accept POAMs for in-progress items?

If you can send an initial package by Nov 5 and we can schedule a 30-min sync this week, that would be great.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Doe
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Analytics

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodai.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FedRAMP / ISO control owner mapping and evidence timeline

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. High level update and proposal:  

- ISO 27001: We are mid-way through a gap remediation sprint focused on policies and access control evidence. We expect to complete the core evidence set for controls in scope by Nov 12 (full certification track continues into Q1).
- FedRAMP: We support Moderate baseline strategies and are aligning technical evidence; however, full FedRAMP package (SSP + POA&M closure) will likely extend past Nov 20 for Moderate. We can provide SSP excerpts and compensating control evidence earlier.

Proposed deliverables: initial evidence-index.csv + control-owner mapping (Nov 5), SOC2 executive summary & sample artifacts (Nov 8), formal attestation/pack for procurement (Nov 12). If FedRAMP Moderate is required as a gate, we should plan a short exception/POAM agreement — we can accept POAMs for noncritical items with agreed remediation windows.

Two clarifying Qs for Acme:  
- Is FedRAMP Moderate a must-have for Nov 20 (hard stop) or is POAM with remediation window acceptable?
- Any specific controls or systems (e.g., on-prem connectors, VPC peering) that you want prioritized?

I'm attaching an index (stub) to start; Marcus and Marissa are looped for control-owner mapping and evidence pulls. Happy to take a call — proposing Thu Nov 5 10:00 PT.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Looping in a draft mapping and a few notes. Attached is a first-pass control-owner spreadsheet that maps SIG/CAIQ controls to our internal owners and where evidence lives (GCS paths). Highlights:  

- Owner assignments: Infra (Vivek) for network and host controls; Runtime (Marcus) for model-serving controls; Platform Security (Marissa) for IAM/policy artifacts.
- Evidence readiness: ~70% of SOC2 artifacts are ready; ISO docs (policy versions) are in review and will be finalized by Nov 10.

Questions for Acme (quick):
- Which FedRAMP baseline — you mentioned Moderate in the initial note, can you confirm?
- Will you accept a POA&M for controls tied to planned infra changes (we estimate 30-60 day remediation on a handful of non-prod controls)?

I attached the control-owner-mapping.xlsx (stub). Irene — happy to join the call on Nov 5 and walk through the spreadsheet.
